answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report via `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>`; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314 % of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping context: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated one, from the LBNL catalogue):
  b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198  (P(M>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719)
  b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922   (P(M>=5.5) observed volume = 0.0002155; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809)
  b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474    (P(M>=5.5) observed volume = 0.0006484; P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653)

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Which is which: the per-b table (b = 1.0 / 0.73 / 0.65) is the CALIBRATED result, derived from the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue via Shapiro et al. (2021) Eq. 5. The single DAS-based number (b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842) is an UPPER BOUND using uncalibrated DAS magnitudes and over-counts, because every DAS detection is treated as an event at or above the catalogue magnitude of completeness. So a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event is very unlikely on the calibrated catalogue basis (0.00012-0.0147 per year depending on b), and at most 0.0784 per year on the conservative DAS upper bound.
